description: Raw bridge command passthrough for anything the named tools don't cover. cmd = the bridge command string; args = an object merged into the request. Returns the frame (if any) or the JSON response.

args.description: Extra fields merged into the request

project.description: Registered project to target. Registry changes apply on the next call; the default project name is pinned at startup (or the first valid registry).

name: defold_bridge

description: Press one or more input triggers in the running game, in order, then return the screen. Trigger ids are the game's action ids from its input bindings (e.g. key_w, key_e, key_space). NOTE: bridge input drives the in-game controller, not the GUI front-end; use defold_start to get past menus first.

project.description: Registered project to target. Registry changes apply on the next call; the default project name is pinned at startup (or the first valid registry).

stop_on.description: Stop the batch after the first key that meets any of these (read from the game's per-key reply); the result says which key and why

triggers.description: Trigger ids pressed in order, e.g. ["key_w","key_w","key_e"]; at most 100 per call

description: Build the target project with the debug bridge enabled and launch it (windowed, detached). Returns when the bridge answers (~30-90s with a build). Pass skip_build=true to relaunch the last build fast. If a bridged game is already running, stop it first with defold_stop.

project.description: Registered project to target. Registry changes apply on the next call; the default project name is pinned at startup (or the first valid registry).

skip_build.description: Skip the build; launch the existing build output (default false)

name: defold_run

description: The running game's current screen as a composed text frame: whatever view the game's bridge composes (an ASCII map + HUD for a glyph game, a score readout for an arcade game).

project.description: Registered project to target. Registry changes apply on the next call; the default project name is pinned at startup (or the first valid registry).

name: defold_screen

description: A picture of the running game's real window (PNG), captured without bringing it to the front. Use it for anything the composed text frame of defold_screen cannot show: fonts, colours, layout, sprites. Windows only. The game redraws on input, so a state changed through defold_bridge may need a key press first.

project.description: Registered project to target. Registry changes apply on the next call; the default project name is pinned at startup (or the first valid registry).

name: defold_screenshot

description: Begin a run, skipping the game's front-end (title menu / character creation) via the bridge `start` command, which GUI input can't reach. `options` is passed through to the game's bridge; what it accepts is per-game (a new-game seed, a character build, a scenario id).

options.description: Game-defined start options, merged into the bridge start request

name: defold_start

description: Compact state of the running game as JSON. Fields are game-defined (position, health, score, flags, whatever the bridge reports).

name: defold_state

description: Quit the running bridged game cleanly (sends the bridge quit command), then wait for the port to be free, and say if it is still held. force=true kills the Defold engine listening on the project's port by its PID (Windows), for a game whose bridge no longer answers; anything that is not a Defold engine is refused.

force.description: Kill the engine on the port by PID instead of asking it to quit (default false)

description: Run the project's headless test suite (if a testScript is registered). Returns the tail of the output when the suite passes; a non-zero exit is a tool ERROR carrying the exit code and the same tail. Widen `tail` when the failing assertion is further up than the default window. Can take minutes.

project.description: Registered project to target. Registry changes apply on the next call; the default project name is pinned at startup (or the first valid registry).

tail.description: Lines from the end of the output (default 12)
